S4-1.reason: Permission addressed to producers about packaging. This implementation uses one representation; nothing follows for a verifier to check.

S4.2-1.note: Exclusion rules may read only issuer attributes or target attributes from the frozen target directory; any other input is a profile error.

S4.3-1.note: Reading: transport acknowledgements are not receiver-side records; they are accounted in the input accounting, outside |R|.

S5.1-6.note: Each obligation lists every attempt that carries evidence; report_check refuses a named attempt missing from that list.

S5.4-1.note: -01 finding S5.4-1 (Disposition when no issuer-side observation exists for an instruction in the population) is resolved in -02: Section 5.4 lines 746-758 define a missing required issuer observation: the instruction stays accounted for, dispatch is NOT_ESTABLISHED, the obligation INDETERMINATE by default. Implemented.

S5.4-7.reason: Addressed to the issuer side (recording a failed emission). The verifier consumes such a record and keeps it as an instruction-level diagnostic; that behaviour is tested under S5.4-8. -01 finding S5.4-5 (result of an emission that failed before the issuer boundary) is resolved by Section 5.4 lines 760-766.

S5.4-8.finding: Disposition of the obligations of an instruction whose only issuer record is an unscoped failed emission
readings: (a) INDETERMINATE: the required issuer observation at the boundary is missing (5.4 default)
(b) UNCONFIRMED: an expected obligation without a matching receiver observation
S5.4-8.implemented: (a), with dispatch NOT_ESTABLISHED and the failure kept as an instruction diagnostic
S5.4-8.why: 5.4 makes a missing issuer observation INDETERMINATE by default and forbids consuming the failure as proof of non-delivery; UNCONFIRMED is defined by the absence of a receiver observation only, while here the issuer side itself is not established.

S5.5-3.note: Reading: an observer absent from the trust configuration gives INDETERMINATE (unresolved trust binding); an observer bound to another target gives an invalid receiver record and leaves the obligation as it was.

S5.7-3.note: -01 finding S5.7-3 (NO_EFFECT is used in two dimensions and the control-effect vocabulary is not defined) is resolved in -02: Sections 4.4 (lines 635-639) and 4.5 (lines 653-658) put enforcement NO_EFFECT and control-effect NO_EFFECT in separate namespaces; the -01 reading (b) stands.

S5.8-1.note: -01 finding S5.8-1 (Deadline-elapsed negative observation: UNCONFIRMED or EXPLICIT_FAILURE) is resolved in -02: Section 5.8 lines 833-836 and 9.1 lines 1692-1694: deadline elapsed leaves UNCONFIRMED with a deadline diagnostic; the -01 reading (a) stands.

S5.8-3.reason: MAY. This verifier defines no timely-delivery claim kind; the deadline diagnostic stays on the obligation, which remains UNCONFIRMED (Section 5.8).

S5.10-8.finding: How a record names the uniqueness scope of its identifier, and which scopes are valid
readings: (a) a record or frozen instruction may carry its own identifier scope; equal strings from different scopes are different identities
(b) only scopes the profile lists are valid; a record of another scope is INVALID
S5.10-8.implemented: (a): an optional identifier_scope; a record of a scope the frozen population does not hold stays outside the population and blocks PASS through the population check
S5.10-8.why: 5.1 asks the profile to define one uniqueness scope; 5.10 speaks of several valid scopes without saying how a record conveys which one it belongs to.

S5.10-10.note: Reduction rule: the profile's published precedence over the seven dispositions; every applicable disposition stays listed.

S5.11-6.reason: Addressed to whoever runs reconciliations. Each report names the exclusion rule versions it applied (S5.11-4) and the digest of the report before it, so a changed rule shows as a separate report; a single verifier run cannot see whether a producer rewrote another run.

S5.11-8.note: -01 finding S5.11-3 (record class of a receiver record that addresses an expected obligation but does not confirm it) is resolved in -02: matched means correlated (Section 5.11 lines 939-947, Section 6.1 lines 1212-1220). A receiver record of an attempt the issuer never emitted is now correlated, not orphan.

S5.11-17.note: Receiver records of an unclosed instruction have no expected obligation to correlate with and are ORPHAN, with the instruction class named.

S5.11-18.note: Known targets of an unclosed resolution are reported as a subscope with its narrower scope stated, outside the Delivery Obligation population.

S5.12-1.finding: Class of an issuer binding that contradicts the frozen Required Target Set
readings: (a) INVALID: the issuer record lacks the binding required for structural validity
(b) CONFLICT: two verified inputs (issuer record and frozen target set) make irreconcilable claims
S5.12-1.implemented: the profile classifies it as INVALID or CONFLICT; the example profile says INVALID. Unresolved, ambiguous and stale references are always INDETERMINATE (the -01 finding S5.12-1 is resolved)
S5.12-1.why: 5.12 names INVALID for a missing required binding and CONFLICT for irreconcilable verified records; a binding to a different set is neither missing nor a second record of the same kind.

S5.14-2.reason: Addressed to a relying system's operational policy (fail-safe, retry, escalation). The report exposes the four states; choosing the local response is outside this verifier.

S6.1-1.note: -01 finding S6.1-1 (Issuer-side identifier reuse with different content) is resolved in -02: Sections 5.10 (lines 879-885) and 6.1 (lines 1190-1196) define SUBSTITUTION for issuer-issuer reuse within one uniqueness scope; the -01 reading (a) stands, now with the records named.

S6.2-1.note: -01 finding S6.2-1 (Parent result of an instruction with zero obligations) is resolved in -02: Section 6.2 lines 1252-1254: parent confirmation of a terminal empty set is NOT_APPLICABLE or absent; the -01 reading (a) stands (null).

S6.3-1.note: Duplicate selection rule: earliest observed time, then record id; the discarded record names the selected one.

S6.4-2.note: -01 finding S6.4-1 (Unit of a Delivery Obligation) is resolved in -02: Sections 2 (lines 354-360), 4.2 (lines 574-579) and 5.1 (lines 687-693) fix the base obligation as instruction times required target; the -01 reading (a) stands.

S6.4-3.note: -01 finding S6.4-3 (Instruction-level equation has no class for a target resolution that fails or stays open) is resolved in -02: Sections 5.11 (lines 983-990) and 6.4 (lines 1365-1374) add the disjoint class target_resolution_unclosed; the instruction equation now has three terms and no obligation is created for an unclosed instruction. Implemented: class renamed, no obligations, one equation.

S6.4-9.note: The matched class is a primary class; its confirming and non-confirming subdivision is published beside the equation and not added to it.

S6.5-2.finding: How an exclusion-rule violation becomes a positive FAIL condition
readings: (a) a positively established invalid or outcome-adaptive exclusion is a FAIL condition the profile may declare
(b) such an exclusion only prevents PASS
S6.5-2.implemented: (b) for this implementation: it finds exclusion-rule violations only as profile declaration errors, under which no FAIL is derived, and refuses a profile that declares them a FAIL condition; the dispositions EXPLICIT_FAILURE, SUBSTITUTION, CONFLICT and INVALID are declared true or false by the profile
S6.5-2.why: 6.5 asks how exclusion-rule violations are handled in the FAIL conditions, while 5.11 says such an exclusion prevents PASS and only a predeclared positive condition produces FAIL; the text does not say what evidence makes the violation positive.

S6.5-5.note: -01 finding S6.5-3 (Which dispositions are positive failing conditions for FAIL) is resolved in -02: Section 6.5 lines 1420-1426: the profile publishes and freezes its positive FAIL conditions; no universal mapping. Implemented as fail_conditions in the profile.

S6.5-6.note: -01 finding S6.5-4 (Excluding an obligation 'before population construction' cannot depend on its disposition) is resolved in -02: Sections 4.2 (lines 565-572) and 5.11 (lines 921-926): exclusions are frozen before receiver evidence and never depend on a disposition; the -01 reading (a) stands.

S6.6-3.note: -01 finding S6.6-3 (Co-exposure when no relying-party claim is requested) is resolved in -02: Section 6.6 lines 1487-1492: with no stronger claim requested, the corresponding claim is the minimal structural statement under the named profile, cutoff and structural rules; the -01 reading (a) stands, the claim scope now names the profile.

S7-1.reason: Addressed to protocol design (attachment points). Not a verifier behaviour.

S9.1-1.reason: Addressed to deployments (deadline definition). Not a verifier behaviour.

S9.1-3.reason: MAY. No timely-delivery claim kind (see S5.8-3).

S9.3-1.reason: Addressed to deployments (binding paths into a Required Target Set). The per-obligation reconciliation it leads to is implemented under S5.10-1.

S9.4-2.note: -01 finding S9.4-2 ('Occurred before control activation' needs an ordering basis) is resolved in -02: Section 9.4 lines 1753-1756: only a crossing whose ordering is supported under Section 5.9 is protected; unsupported ordering is omitted or INDETERMINATE; the -01 reading (a) stands.

S11-1.reason: Privacy practice for implementations in deployment. Not a verifier behaviour; the vectors carry no personal data.

S11-2.reason: Privacy default for producers. Not a verifier behaviour; vectors carry only small synthetic instruction content.

S11-3.reason: Privacy practice for profiles (commitments, nonces). Not implemented; digests here are unsalted and the vectors use synthetic content.
